tool.name: SEM fiber analysis
tool.description: segment fibers and measure their diameters with FIJI and DiameterJ
tool.command: mkdir -p results && export ANALYSIS_RESULTS_DIR='results' && ln -s '$input_image' input.tif && /usr/local/bin/sem-analysis --input input.tif --output results --method '$method' --crop-bottom '$advanced.crop_bottom' #if $calibration.source == 'pixel_size': --pixel-size-um '$calibration.pixel_size_um' #else: --hfw-um '$calibration.hfw_um' #end if --sigma '$advanced.sigma' --min-object-px '$advanced.min_object_px' --min-hole-px '$advanced.min_hole_px' #if $advanced.invert: --invert #end if #if $analysis_mode == 'qc': --skip-diameterj #end if #if $analysis_mode == 'diameterj': && python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; from PIL import Image; source = Path('results/input__${method}_Radius Plot.tif'); Image.open(source).save(source.with_suffix('.png')); source.unlink()" #end if

param.name: input_image
param.label: SEM micrograph
param.help: A 2-D TIFF image. RGB TIFFs are converted to grayscale.

validator.message: Horizontal field width must be greater than zero
Pixel size must be greater than zero

param.name: crop_bottom
param.label: Crop from bottom (pixels)
param.help: Removes the SEM instrument footer before analysis.

param.name: invert
param.label: Fibers are darker than the background

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool prepares an SEM micrograph for DiameterJ, creates a binary fiber mask, and computes an independent Python diameter quality-control estimate. In full mode it also runs the validated DiameterJ 1.018 workflow under a virtual display.
Processing consists of optional footer removal, adaptive contrast enhancement, Gaussian smoothing, global thresholding, removal of small objects, filling of small holes, skeletonization, and distance-transform diameter measurement.
**Input image**
The input must be a TIFF image. A two-dimensional grayscale image is used directly. An RGB TIFF is converted to grayscale by averaging its first three channels. Other dimensional layouts, such as image stacks or time series, are not supported.
**Global threshold method**
The threshold separates fibers from the background after contrast enhancement and smoothing. No one method is optimal for every micrograph.
* **Otsu** minimizes variance within the foreground and background classes. It is a useful default for images with two reasonably distinct intensity groups. * **Li** iteratively minimizes cross-entropy. It can work well when the two intensity classes overlap or the histogram is asymmetric. * **Yen** maximizes a histogram-based correlation criterion. It may preserve bright, fine structures but can select more foreground in noisy images. * **Triangle** estimates a threshold from the shape of a skewed histogram. It is often useful when fibers occupy a relatively small fraction of the image.
Inspect the binary mask and overlay when selecting a method. The same method is used in both QC-only and full DiameterJ modes.
**Analysis mode**
* **Full DiameterJ analysis** creates the Python segmentation and QC results, then runs DiameterJ 1.018. This is the primary analysis mode and produces ten result files. * **Segmentation and Python QC only** skips DiameterJ. It is faster and produces four files, making it useful for testing thresholds and cleanup parameters.
**Calibration and interpretation**
Python QC measurements are reported in pixels and micrometres. Choose one of the following calibration sources:
* **Horizontal field width** is the physical width represented by the entire uncropped image. Pixel size is calculated as ``HFW / image width in pixels``. The default is 27.04 µm and should be replaced with the value recorded by the microscope for the input image. * **Pixel size** directly specifies micrometres per pixel. Use this when the calibrated pixel spacing is already known.
Cropping the bottom does not change image width, so it does not alter an HFW-derived pixel size. DiameterJ runs in its validated native-pixel mode because physical calibration can change its legacy particle-size filtering. Use the ``pixel_size_um`` field in ``python_qc_summary.csv`` when converting DiameterJ measurements to physical units.
**Segmentation options**
* **Crop from bottom** removes a fixed number of pixel rows before analysis. The default of 59 is intended for an SEM annotation or instrument footer. Set it to 0 when the image contains no footer. It must be smaller than image height. * **Gaussian denoising sigma** controls smoothing before thresholding. A larger value suppresses more fine-scale noise but may merge nearby fibers or erase thin structures. A value of 0 disables Gaussian smoothing. * **Minimum fiber object area** removes connected foreground regions smaller than the specified number of pixels. Increase it to reject isolated specks; decrease it to retain small fibers. * **Minimum filled-hole area** fills background holes within the fiber mask up to the specified pixel area. Increase it to close more small gaps, but avoid values that fill genuine pores. * **Fibers are darker than the background** reverses the threshold comparison. Leave it disabled for bright fibers on a dark background; enable it for dark fibers on a bright background.
Object and hole limits are areas in pixels, not linear dimensions. Their physical effect therefore depends on image calibration and magnification.
**Outputs**
All generated files are returned as one list collection in the Galaxy history. Dataset names retain the input stem and threshold method. QC-only mode includes the mask TIFF, segmentation overlay PNG, diameter samples CSV, and Python QC summary CSV. Full mode additionally includes the DiameterJ total summary, comparison image, pore data, radius histogram, characteristic lengths, and the radius plot converted to PNG.
The QC diameter samples are distance-transform measurements on skeleton pixels. They are intended as an independent quality check; DiameterJ output is the primary result in full-analysis mode.
